🏥 Rotary Friendship Exchange – Visit to a Centre for Persons with Disabilities

Learning from Community-Based Rehabilitation Initiatives in Argentina

Rotary Club of Bombay Uptown | District 3141, India
Rotary Friendship Exchange 2026–27 | Argentina

As part of the Rotary Friendship Exchange to Argentina, the delegation from Rotary Club of Bombay Uptown, District 3141, visited a centre in América, Rivadavia, Buenos Aires Province, dedicated to the development, rehabilitation and support of persons with disabilities.

The visit provided valuable insight into a community initiative established through collaboration between Rotary Club de América, the Municipality of Rivadavia and the parents’ association “Por un mundo mejor.” The facility’s inauguration plaque records the opening of its first phase on 2 May 2014, under the Participatory Budget 2012 initiative.

During the visit, the delegation was briefed on the centre’s development, the equipment required for its operations and the role of Rotary Global Grant support in helping meet essential equipment needs. The discussion also highlighted the pending work required to further complete and enhance the facility for the benefit of persons with disabilities.

The interaction offered an important opportunity to understand the challenges involved in developing specialised facilities and the value of partnerships between Rotary, local authorities and community organisations. It reinforced the importance of sustained support to ensure that persons with disabilities have access to appropriate facilities for rehabilitation, development and improved quality of life.

For the visiting Rotarians, the experience was both informative and inspiring. It demonstrated how collaborative service projects can create meaningful community infrastructure, while also reminding us that the completion and long-term sustainability of such initiatives are essential to maximising their impact.

Inclusion • Rehabilitation • Dignity • Sustainable Service

The visit strengthened the spirit of international learning and friendship between District 3141, India, and District 4895, Argentina, reaffirming Rotary’s commitment to building inclusive communities where every individual has the opportunity to thrive.
